mechanism_narrative: The strong upward trend observed in RETAIL_REC over the last week indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, leading to higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite the observed upward trend in the last week.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the most recent data, signals a return to office and daily routines, which will directly boost retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a broader shift towards out-of-home activities, which will positively influence retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and GROCERY_PHARM rises week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, even when RESIDENTIAL mobility falls and GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in TRANSIT mobility, reflecting increased public transport usage, indicates greater overall movement and accessibility to commercial areas, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite a continued upward trend in TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility, as seen in the latest data, suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure, potentially redirecting discretionary activity towards indoor retail and recreation venues over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 7 days following a week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility greater than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signifies a robust return to pre-pandemic routines, including commuting and associated retail spending, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite concurrent increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates that people are spending less time at home, thereby increasing their availability and likelihood to engage in out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, even as RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility is positive and consistently rising, it reflects a general comfort with out-of-home activities, which serves as a leading indicator for increased discretionary retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is positive and rising for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility being positive and rising for two consecutive weeks.
